rtk.title: RTK Compression Configuration
rtk.subtitle: Automatically compress tool outputs and code blocks to reduce token usage and latency
rtk.enableDescription: Compress tool outputs to reduce token usage and latency
rtk.enableSubDescription: When off, every request passes through uncompressed. Useful for A/B-comparing tool-output cost vs. quality.
rtk.formErrorToast: Please fix the form errors before submitting
rtk.noDataYet: No compression activity yet — counters reset on gateway restart
rtk.introDescription: RTK automatically compresses tool outputs and code blocks around every LLM request, cutting cost and latency. Sections below go from daily-use to advanced; 80% of users just pick a preset.
rtk.introBullet1: Pre-LLM: shrinks tool outputs before they reach the model
rtk.introBullet2: Post-LLM: cleans up accumulated tool outputs after the request, keeping what can be reconstructed
rtk.introBullet3: Fail-open: on any compression error, the original text is sent unchanged — never breaks a request
rtk.presetHelp: Click a preset to fill in a sensible group of values; you can still tweak any field afterwards.
rtk.presetAppliedToast: Applied '{{name}}' preset — you can fine-tune before saving
rtk.revertPresetToast: Reverted preset fields to last saved values
rtk.presetMinimalHint: Keeps more context; saves fewer tokens
rtk.presetAggressiveHint: Maximum compression; trades context for the lowest token count
rtk.afterSaveBody: After saving, use Preview or Test Runner to compare compressed vs uncompressed on the same input. To inspect de-redacted raw output, temporarily switch retention to "On Failures" or "Always" and use the Raw Output viewer.
rtk.intensityDescription: Controls how aggressive compression is. Scales the line/char budgets below proportionally.
rtk.intensityWhen: Raise it when tool outputs are huge and the model only needs the gist; lower it when you need more context to avoid misjudgement.
rtk.maxLinesDescription: Maximum lines to keep per tool result after compression
rtk.maxLinesWhen: Raise if the model keeps missing key info in the middle; lower to save tokens when the model doesn't need that much detail.
rtk.maxCharsDescription: Maximum characters to keep per tool result after compression
rtk.maxCharsWhen: Prevents one tool result from filling the whole context window. Raise slightly if long outputs are getting truncated too aggressively.
rtk.dedupThresholdDescription: Number of consecutive identical lines before deduplication kicks in
rtk.dedupThresholdWhen: Lower this (e.g. 2 or 3) when tool output contains long runs of identical lines (e.g. repeated failure logs, infinite-loop output); otherwise keep the default of 3.
rtk.enableGroupingDescription: Fuzzy-group near-equivalent consecutive lines (only differ in timestamps/hex IDs/numbers/versions)
rtk.enableGroupingWhen: Turn on when tool output has long runs of lines that differ only in timestamp/number/version (time-series logs, build artifact lists, etc.) — it kills a lot of noise.
rtk.groupingThresholdDescription: Minimum run length of near-equivalent lines before grouping kicks in
rtk.groupingThresholdWhen: Default 3 is fine. Lower it to merge sparser similar lines; raise it to avoid merging legitimately different lines.
rtk.enableRenderersDescription: Rewrite structured outputs (git diff, test suites, terraform plan, JSON tables) into a more compact form after line filtering. Fail-open: a no-op or panic leaves the text unchanged
rtk.enableRenderersWhen: Turn on when the team heavily uses git diff / pytest / terraform plan and the like — second-stage compaction is much more stable. Fail-open means there's no risk in enabling it.
rtk.disabledRenderersDescription: Listed detection types are not rewritten by semantic compression. Empty (default) enables every registered renderer when 'Enable semantic compression' is on
rtk.disabledRenderersWhen: Pick a specific type to skip (e.g. don't rewrite git diff); leave empty for "all on".
rtk.disabledRenderersLoadError: Failed to load the renderer catalog. Refresh to retry; you can still type detection type names by hand for now.
rtk.disabledRenderersUnknownWarning: These detection types are not in the built-in catalog: {{names}}. They have been preserved as-is (so they will not be skipped), but consider switching to the canonical name from the dropdown to make sure they actually take effect.
rtk.rawOutputRetentionDescription: Controls when raw tool outputs are persisted to disk. When non-Never, the gateway embeds a capability URL (no Authorization header required) in the tool_result so the LLM can recover the original via GET. The 24-character hex id is itself the capability (96 bits of entropy) and expires after Raw Output TTL; anyone with the id can read until then.
rtk.rawOutputRetentionWhen: Keep "Never" for day-to-day to save disk; switch to "On Failures" or "Always" while debugging, then read the de-redacted text from the Raw Output viewer.
rtk.rawOutputMaxBytesDescription: Caps the persisted raw output size in bytes
rtk.rawOutputMaxBytesWhen: When retention is "Always", consider lowering this (default 1 MB) so disk doesn't fill up; restore the default after debugging.
rtk.rawOutputDirDescription: Override the on-disk root for raw-output persistence. Leave empty to use the server default.
rtk.rawOutputDirWhen: When set, must be an absolute path. Operators usually point this at a dedicated volume or tmpfs so cleanup is bounded.
rtk.rawOutputTTLDescription: How long raw-output files live on disk before the janitor reaps them. 0 disables the janitor.
rtk.rawOutputTTLWhen: Default 24 hours. Range 0-168 (1 week). LLM clients can recover truncated tool_result via the /api/context/rtk/raw-output/<id> endpoint as long as the file is still on disk.
rtk.snapshotModeDescription: Controls whether the pre-compression text is saved to the "Log detail → RTK Compression" tab
rtk.snapshotModeWhen: Switch to "Per-message" when you want to compare each message before/after; keep "Disabled" (default) to save storage when log volume is high.
rtk.snapshotMaxBytesWhen: Raise if you see snapshots being truncated under heavy compression; lower to strictly cap log storage.
rtk.minTokensToCompressDescription: Skip compression when estimated request tokens are below this threshold (0 = never skip)
rtk.minTokensToCompressWhen: Raise it to skip compression on small requests and save processing time; set to 0 if your agentic workflow always involves high-token requests.
rtk.cavemanIntro: Rule-based compression for user-role prose (chat messages). Complements RTK (which targets tool output). Enabled from the pipeline checkbox in the enablement card above.
rtk.cavemanIntensityWhen: lite keeps only safe filler removals; full adds articles/leaders/structural rewrites; ultra adds aggressive abbreviations.
rtk.cavemanIntensityDescription: Higher intensities remove more tokens but rewrite more aggressively.
rtk.cavemanMinLengthWhen: Messages shorter than this (in characters/runes) pass through unchanged to avoid churn on small turns.
rtk.cavemanMinLengthDescription: Minimum message length before a user message is eligible for compression (default 50).
rtk.cavemanSkipRulesWhen: Built-in rules to disable. The dropdown lets you search and group by category; you can still type a name by hand (e.g. for rules added in future releases). Useful when a rule over-fires on your domain text.
rtk.cavemanSkipRulesDescription: Rule names that never run. Empty = all rules enabled.
rtk.cavemanSkipRulesUnknownWarning: These rule names are not in the built-in catalog: {{names}}. They have been preserved as-is (so they will not run), but consider switching to the canonical name from the dropdown to make sure they actually take effect.
rtk.cavemanSkipRulesLoadError: Failed to load the built-in rule catalog. Refresh to retry; you can still type rule names by hand for now.
rtk.cavemanPreserveWhen: Extra regexes (in addition to the built-in 17) for regions to protect from compression, e.g. THE_BRAND_NAME.
rtk.cavemanPreserveDescription: Comma-separated regexes whose matches stay verbatim through compression.
rtk.cavemanPreserveBuiltInHint: The categories below are already protected by default — you usually don't need to repeat them.
rtk.cavemanPreserveUnknownWarning: {{count}} pattern(s) failed to compile. Check the regex syntax.

cavemanRule.redundant_phrasing: Collapse 'make sure to', 'be sure to', 'it is important to', 'you should', 'remember to', etc. into direct phrasing.
cavemanRule.pleasantries: Strip conversational openers and closers like 'thanks', 'happy to', 'certainly', 'glad to help'.
cavemanRule.polite_framing: Remove 'please', 'kindly', 'could you please' style politeness wrappers.
cavemanRule.hedging: Cut hedging like 'I think that', 'probably', 'maybe it', 'it appears that'.
cavemanRule.verbose_instructions: Shorten 'provide a detailed explanation of' / 'write an in-depth' down to 'explain'.
cavemanRule.filler_adverbs: Strip adverbs that don't add meaning: basically, essentially, actually, literally, simply, currently.
cavemanRule.filler_phrases: Remove 'I want to' / 'I'd like to' style lead-ins on user messages.
cavemanRule.redundant_openers: Strip greetings at the start of user messages: 'Hi there', 'Hello', 'Hey'.
cavemanRule.verbose_requests: Cut 'I was wondering if you could' / 'Would it be possible to' hedges on user requests.
cavemanRule.self_reference: Remove 'I am trying to' / 'I am working on' / 'I have been' style self-reference lead-ins.
cavemanRule.excessive_gratitude: Strip multi-word thanks: 'Thank you so much', 'Thanks in advance', 'I really appreciate'.
cavemanRule.qualifier_removal: Remove soft quantifiers: a bit, a little, somewhat, kind of, sort of.
cavemanRule.softeners: Strip politeness softeners like 'when you get a chance', 'just wondering'.
cavemanRule.uncertainty_fillers: Cut 'I guess', 'I suppose', 'more or less', 'in a way'.
cavemanRule.assistant_fillers: Strip 'Here's' / 'Below is' / 'This is' lead-ins from assistant messages.
cavemanRule.articles: Drop 'a', 'an', 'the' before words when it doesn't change meaning.
cavemanRule.leader_phrases: Compress 'I will' / 'let me' / 'let's' / 'you can' leading phrases to bare verbs.
cavemanRule.explanatory_prefix: Rewrite 'The function appears to be handling' / 'The code seems to' to 'Function:' / 'Code:'.
cavemanRule.question_to_directive: Convert 'Can you explain why' style questions into direct imperatives.
cavemanRule.context_setup: Replace 'Here is my code' / 'Below is the code' with 'Code:'.
cavemanRule.intent_clarification: Replace 'What I'm trying to do is' / 'My objective is to' with 'Goal:'.
cavemanRule.background_removal: Strip 'As you may know' / 'As we discussed earlier' filler.
cavemanRule.meta_commentary: Drop 'Note that' / 'Keep in mind that' / 'Remember that' meta-instructions.
cavemanRule.purpose_statement: Shorten 'for the purpose of' / 'with the goal of' to 'for' / 'to'.
cavemanRule.list_conjunction: Collapse 'and also' / 'as well as' to a comma.
cavemanRule.purpose_phrases: Replace 'in order to' / 'so as to' with 'to'.
cavemanRule.redundant_quantifiers: Tighten 'each and every' / 'any and all' to 'each' / 'all'.
cavemanRule.transition_removal: Strip leading 'On the other hand' / 'In contrast' / 'However'.
cavemanRule.emphasis_removal: Remove emphasis adverbs: very, really, extremely, highly, quite.
cavemanRule.passive_voice: Rewrite common passive forms ('is being used', 'was created') to active voice.
cavemanRule.redundant_because: Replace 'due to the fact that' with 'because'.
cavemanRule.redundant_directive: Strip 'it is important to' / 'you should' / 'remember to' directives.
cavemanRule.repeated_context: Replace 'As we discussed earlier' style call-backs with 'See above.'
cavemanRule.reestablished_context: Replace 'Going back to the code above' / 'Referring back to' with 'Re:'.
cavemanRule.summary_replacement: Replace 'To summarize what we've discussed' / 'To recap' with 'Summary:'.
cavemanRule.ultra_abbreviations: Abbreviate long technical words (database → DB, configuration → config, function → fn, etc.).
cavemanRule.zh_filler_please: Strip Chinese politeness lead-ins: 请, 请你, 请您, 请帮我, 请帮忙.
cavemanRule.zh_filler_thanks: Strip Chinese thanks: 谢谢, 多谢, 感谢, 谢谢你, 感谢大家.
cavemanRule.zh_filler_trouble: Strip Chinese trouble-apology wrappers: 麻烦你, 麻烦您, 劳驾.
cavemanRule.zh_filler_greeting: Strip Chinese greetings: 你好, 您好, 大家好.
cavemanRule.zh_filler_hedge_think: Cut Chinese hedging: 我觉得, 我认为, 我想说.
cavemanRule.zh_filler_hedge_actually: Cut Chinese 'actually' hedging: 其实, 说实话, 基本上.
cavemanRule.zh_repeated_context: Replace Chinese 'as discussed earlier' call-backs with 见上.
cavemanRule.zh_repeated_question: Tag Chinese repeat questions with ［同问］.
cavemanRule.zh_reestablished_context: Replace Chinese 'going back to' call-backs with Re:.
cavemanRule.zh_summary_replacement: Replace Chinese 'to summarize' lead-ins with 总结：.
cavemanRule.zh_ultra_modal_particles: Drop Chinese modal particles (吗, 呢, 吧, 啊, 呀, 嘛) before sentence-final punctuation.
cavemanRule.zh_ultra_application_abbreviation: Abbreviate 应用程序 to app.
cavemanRule.zh_ultra_dependency_abbreviation: Abbreviate 依赖关系 to dep.
cavemanRule.zh_ultra_config_file_abbreviation: Abbreviate 配置文件 to cfg.

providerCooldown.title: Provider Cooldown Configuration
providerCooldown.enableDescription: Automatically cool down providers that return quota errors
providerCooldown.perProviderPoliciesHint: Each provider can override cooldown_policy independently. Providers without a custom policy fall back to the built-in default. Full editing lives on the provider detail page.
providerCooldown.defaultTTLDescription: Seconds before a cooled-down provider key is automatically re-enabled (1–86400)
providerCooldown.allProvidersConsumed: All configured providers already have an override
providerCooldown.quotaPatternsDescription: Error message patterns that trigger cooldown (at least 1 required)
providerCooldown.formErrorToast: Please fix the form errors before submitting
providerCooldown.noActiveKeys: No keys are currently in cooldown

howItWorks.title: How Cooldown Works
howItWorks.triggerBody: After a provider request fails, the error's message, code, and type are matched (case-insensitively) against the built-in patterns (insufficient_quota, quota exceeded, quota_exceeded, billing, usage limit) plus any custom quota_patterns. Status codes gate the scan: HTTP 429 and other 4xx qualify when the text matches; HTTP 402 (permanent billing failure) and 5xx errors never trigger a cooldown.
howItWorks.effectTitle: What happens while a key is cooling down
howItWorks.effectBody: The failing (provider, key) pair is temporarily removed from the key pool for the configured TTL (default 300 seconds). At key selection the cooled key is skipped, so requests fall through to other healthy keys of the same provider, then to fallback providers. If every eligible key is suppressed, the request fails with a synthetic 429 no_eligible_keys error and a Retry-After response header hinting when the soonest cooldown lapses so clients can retry.
howItWorks.recoveryBody: The key is automatically re-enabled when its TTL expires. Cooldown state lives in process memory, so restarting celer-route clears all cooldowns.
